You are a senior frontend engineer with excellent product taste. Rebuild the web app's main experience to match an approved minimal design ("Sunday flow"): phone first, one decision at a time, calm. Demo today 14:00 (hand-in 12:00), so ship something polished and reliable in ~2 hours. Work directly in the repo; do NOT commit or push. You own web/ (all of web/src, web/index.html, web/public styles); do not edit Python except where noted. Another engineer edits only Python files under src/ask_soony/verifier/ and src/ask_soony/dispatch/ in parallel.

Repo /Users/jonasstenglein/OtherProjects/StartMunichHack/ask-soony; React 19, Tailwind v4, lucide-react, radix Sheet; no new npm packages. The app is served live at :8000 from web/dist (login form /login; password ASK_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD in .env, never print it); `npm run build` updates it.

THE DESIGN (exact reference, open the HTML and screenshots): /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/brand/screens/21-decision.html, 22-source-open.html, 23-done.html, 24-all-clear.html, 25-desktop-focus.html, 20-lockscreen-push.html and shots/20..25-*.png (phone 2x). Rules: one typeface, Instrument Sans (Google Fonts link in index.html with a system fallback), three sizes per viewport (desktop ~34/18/13.5, phone ~27/17/13), plain light ground, one blue for the primary button, red ONLY on the late/short number, the highlighter ONLY on source crops, the routine green ONLY on the routine line, no boxes/chips/pills/KPIs/timeline on the main screen, whitespace instead of borders.

SCREENS:
1. TODAY (route /, phone and desktop): top line "Trucks leave in 13 h 30 min · N decisions" (countdown from state.clock.launch; fall back gracefully). Then the ONE most urgent open decision (state.inbox_ids order / level / deadline): small grey meta "<supplier> · decide by 10:00"; big plain headline (shorten long headlines: prefer a sentence built from card fields: e.g. "<number> <part_name> will arrive after launch." when kind/arrives_at say so; otherwise card.headline without part codes); one sentence with the contradiction built from the system vs document evidence sides ("SAP expects 48,000 by Saturday, but Hwaseong's shipping advice says 20,000 arrive Tue 24 Nov.") where each number is a TAPPABLE grounded citation (reuse web/src/components/SourceAnchors.tsx: useAnchors, CitedText logic, the page/table/scan views with highlight boxes) opening:
2. SOURCE SHEET (bottom sheet on phone, side or centered panel on desktop): the highlighted crop of the document (PDF page/scan/table row with boxes), the original-language line + English translation when present, and beneath it the other side ("SAP says 48,000 due Sat 21 Nov · purchase order line"), "Open original" link, one Back.
   Then "For today: <what it means>" (from state.clock.editions stops_at/runs_dry for the card's edition: "Standard runs out of cards at 17:00, three hours before the trucks"; omit if unknown). Then "We recommend" + the recommended option's action and cost in one sentence; one big primary "Approve" (calls the existing POST /api/cards/{id}/approve with option index; show a confirm line if the option costs money: "Approve: <action> (<cost>)"), quiet "Talk it through" (existing VoiceCall component, keep the ringing ?talk=1 deep link on /d/<id>) and "Other options" (expands the alternatives, Escalate, Dismiss).
3. DONE (after a decision, button or voice): "Done. <what happened>" (e.g. "Asked Boise for 20,000 cards." from the action/status) with a quiet Undo when possible (POST /api/routines/actions/{action_id}/undo exists; show its reason if refused), then EITHER the routine offer when similar open cards exist (group look-alikes like web/src/lib/decisions.ts does: "3 more like this from PackRight. Handle them the same way? You'll see a test run first. Money still comes to you." → "Show me how" opens the existing Routines sheet with `request={cardId,k}` so it drafts a routine; "Not now") OR the next decision ("Next: <headline>" → continue), OR all clear.
4. ALL CLEAR (no open decisions for me): "Nothing needs you." / "On track for the trucks at 20:00." (or the honest status if an edition stops) / "Watching N shipments · see" / the green line "N handled by your routines overnight · see · undo" (count activity items with via starting "routine:"). This is the hero state; make it beautiful.
5. DESKTOP (≥1024 px): the same calm: a very quiet left list (max ~5 one-line items: dot + headline + time, then "+N more"), the focus column (max ~640 px) with the same decision content, the routine line at the bottom. No timeline, no map on this screen.
6. NAVIGATION: minimal top bar: logo mark + "Ask Soony", and a quiet menu (or text links on desktop): Today · Plan · Routines · Suppliers · (bell for alerts). "Plan" = the existing LaunchTimeline + the full decision list (keep DecisionList/DecisionPane as the "all decisions" view, restyled calmer if cheap), "Routines" = the existing Routines sheet/tab (keep all routines features: flow, edit, trust, proposals, drafts), "Suppliers" = the existing SupplyMap. Keep AlertsButton (enable alerts), the /d/<id> deep link (now renders the Today decision view for that card, incl. ringing for ?talk=1), login unaffected.
7. Routine proposals waiting for OK and voice drafts: one quiet line on Today ("Your routines want to do 2 things · review") linking to Routines.
Keep accessibility (real buttons/links, focus states, aria labels), keyboard on desktop (j/k next/prev decision, a = approve with confirm, Esc), no layout shift on the 5 s poll, selection stable.

Data: GET /api/state (cards with headline, number, number_label, part_name, arrives_at, deadline, runs_dry, level, status, supplier_name, options[], evidence[] (system/document sides via source labels), ui (reply...), edition), clock {launch, editions[]}, activity[] (via, action_id), inbox_ids, shipments[]. Read web/src/lib/api.ts, lib/decisions.ts, components/*.
Never click Approve/Escalate/Dismiss/accept on real data in your checks (real supplier emails!); use Playwright page.route to mock /api/state and POSTs. Verify: cd web && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json && npm run build; screenshots at 390x844 and 1440x900 for Today, source open, done (mocked), all clear (mocked), desktop, Plan, Routines into /Users/jonasstenglein/.claude/jobs/3021cc1a/tmp/today/. Compare against the design shots and iterate until they match in calm and hierarchy. Final report: what changed, what was removed from the main screen and where it lives now, screenshots.
